title: LeanMem: Simple and Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents

visual_explainer.blocker: The available GitHub write connector supports UTF-8 text files but exposes no binary-upload action, so the required WebP cannot be committed to main in this run.

analysis.tldr: LeanMem stores different kinds of dialogue evidence differently—stable profile facts, evolving events, and source-grounded records—and plans retrieval over those stores instead of forcing all history into one memory representation.
analysis.problem: Long-term agent histories mix facts with very different temporal dynamics and fidelity requirements; a single summarization or retrieval policy either wastes tokens or destroys information needed later.
analysis.core_idea: Filter low-value dialogue, route retained information into profile, event, or record memory based on its semantics, evolve only the temporal event store, and assemble evidence with query-specific memory-type and token budgets.

memory_design.write: Filter low-information content, segment conversations by topic, and route useful evidence into representation-specific memory types.
memory_design.organize: Separate stable profile memory, temporally evolving event memory, and source-grounded records rather than using one homogeneous store.
memory_design.read: Adaptive Evidence Composition decides which memory types to consult and how much evidence to retrieve for each query.
memory_design.update_forget: Only event memory is selectively evolved as new temporal evidence arrives; stable profile and source-grounded records follow different update semantics.

compared_to: MemoryOS and A-MEM-style long-term memory systems
analysis.evidence: The paper evaluates LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with GPT-4.1-mini and Qwen3-8B backbones. It reports gains over the strongest memory baseline of up to 5.54 points on LoCoMo and 15.07 points on LongMemEval-S depending on the backbone. Ablations show the heterogeneous storage schedule is the largest contributor, with memory evolution and retrieval planning also helping.
analysis.why_it_matters: The important idea is the storage contract: heterogeneous evidence should have heterogeneous lifecycle semantics. That is a more scalable design principle than continuously improving one universal vector-memory abstraction.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to dialogue-memory QA rather than agents taking consequential actions in changing environments.
Routing quality depends on correctly inferring the information type and temporal dynamics of each observation.
The reported evidence does not establish behavior under months- or years-long histories with distribution shifts and conflicting updates.
